Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake dogfish target policy. I’ll first read the workspace contract, then the skill instructions and prescribed rollout keyframes before touching `solver/`; the no-Bookshelf boundary will be maintained.

The workspace contract confirms a single editable candidate file and forbids local CFD. I’m now anchoring the visual comparison to the assigned-parent guidance, all sampled scores/observations/metrics, and inherited optimization notes; then I’ll inspect the shared prewarm plus the strongest and most diagnostic rollout sheets.

The visual/metric comparison isolates the next candidate: the signed fore/aft gate is the only sampled terminal discriminator that preserved—and slightly improved—the useful upstream leg, but zeroing bearing alone still ended in the same nose-up exit. I’ll record a missing-factorial hypothesis before editing: keep bearing shut off after the target passes abeam and simultaneously apply the already-sampled bounded rearward-only turn damping, while leaving the target-ahead gait exactly unchanged.

The single candidate is now implemented as one smooth fore/aft terminal mode, and the durable guidance has been materially revised with the new sampled comparison and its falsification boundary. I’m checking the exact diff, parameter schema, and prescribed runner configuration next; no CFD will be launched.

The prescribed guidance check found a workspace metadata defect: the same assigned parent is marked twice in the rendered `README.md`, so the checker cannot identify exactly one parent. I’m removing only that duplicate marker, then rerunning the check unchanged.

The guidance check passes. The lightweight Julia contract command is currently blocked because this execution image has no `julia` on `PATH` (the preceding SSH-profile warnings are unrelated). I’ll check only the workspace/tool environment for an available Julia binary, then continue with the deterministic schema and boundary checks.

All prescribed checks now pass: the guidance/notes semantic check, the Julia policy-contract execution, and the solver boundary check. The boundary confirms that exactly the permitted target-policy file changed under `solver/`; no CFD was run.

Produced exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): preserves target-ahead propulsion, then smoothly removes aliased bearing and adds bounded turn damping after the target passes abeam.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records the visual diagnosis, evidence, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:100): materially revised with the fore/aft-gating lesson and range-opening negative result.

All prescribed checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary. No CFD was run. I also removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that initially prevented the guidance checker from resolving the parent.
